messages:
Sarah: heads up — saw a weird quota spike this morning after a customer moved a service account from project A -> project B. looks like routing stuck to old project for ~9m and ate their project quota :frowning_face:
Ken: ugh. which layer sticky-ness are we observing? edge cache? auth-proxy?
Sarah: initial guess is the routing cache in auth-proxy. logs show requests still tagged with origin_project=A even though token is for B
Devin: do we have the raw header dump? maybe token exchange path leaves behind an origin header we don't overwrite
Sarah: pasted minimal example from the proxy logs:
```
RequestId: 01EXAMPLE
Authorization: Bearer eyJ...
X-Org-Origin: project-A
X-Forwarded-For: 10.2.3.4
```
After exchange, exchange service returned project=B but proxy cache key was still using X-Org-Origin
Riley: so cache key is currently: <api_key_id>:<X-Org-Origin> right? that's bad if headers can lag after exchange
Ken: yup. current code: cacheKey := fmt.Sprintf("%s:%s", keyID, r.Header.Get("X-Org-Origin"))
Devin: quick mitigation: prefer authoritative origin from introspection response, fall back to header only if introspect unavailable. set cache TTL low for ephemeral tokens (30s)
Sarah: agree. question for console folks — how do we surface this to users? they saw quotas burn and dashboard showed traffic under old project for a bit
Riley: UX idea — add a small banner on quota dashboard when any request retention shows sudden project-affinity flip with a link to incidents. also surface sample request IDs so support can trace
Ken: telemetry ask: emit metric auth.proxy.cache_miss_reason with tag reason=(stale-header|introspect-fail|no-introspect) and include original vs resolved project in logs (sampled)
Devin: implementation plan:
- short term: change cache key to prefer introspect.project when present (rollout immediate)
- medium: set ephemeral token TTL override to 30s via config flag
- long term: update console to annotate affected quota buckets and add banner
Canary: roll to 10% of auth-proxy pods in prod region us-west1 then monitor cache_miss_reason and per-project token attribution graph
Sarah: sounds good. any concerns about introspect latency increasing request p95?
Ken: introspect is fairly fast (<15ms) but do a perf run. if it adds tail latency we can do async refresh with a short fallback TTL on the cache
Riley: support playbook note: when customer reports quota burn after migration, check metric project_attribution_diff and query sample request IDs from logs. add as KB article
Sarah: I'll open a small PR for the cache-key change and attach perf numbers. tagging @deploy-bot to kick off canary once merged
deploy-bot: deploy queued: auth-proxy-canary -> 10% -> us-west1. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/pulls/1234 :rocket:
Ken: thanks all — let's keep monitoring tomorrow morning and follow up in #incidents if we see recurrence :+1:
